episode_title: From blogger to billionaire, Canva's co-founder on what failures at Google Wave taught him
question: What was Google Wave and why was it eventually shut down despite its technological innovation?
transcript_excerpt: Google Wave was a communications product that combined real-time communication, seamless docs, spreadsheets, and chat into one product. Although the underlying technology was incredibly impressive and influenced products like Slack and Google Docs, it was not a great success at launch because people couldn't figure out how to weave it into their day-to-day lives. Eventually the team gave up on it, though its legacy was significant in shaping how people collaborate in real time today.

episode_title: From blogger to billionaire, Canva's co-founder on what failures at Google Wave taught him
question: How did Canva's approach to product launch differ from the lean startup methodology popular at the time?
transcript_excerpt: While The Lean Startup methodology advocated getting products out quickly to learn from users, Canva deliberately spent a year building and testing before launch. Cameron and his co-founders knew they needed to launch a product with a certain level of quality based on their understanding of users from past experience in design and technology. Despite investors constantly telling them to launch, they built something they knew their customers would love, and when they did go live, they had all the signals that people would really like it.

episode_title: From blogger to billionaire, Canva's co-founder on what failures at Google Wave taught him
question: What happened when Fluent unexpectedly gained 80,000 users in one day and what were the business consequences?
transcript_excerpt: After a journalist published a front-page story about Fluent, 80,000 people descended wanting to use the product in just one day, though the team wasn't ready for the surge. Running the product for all those users would have cost $400,000 in the first month alone, which they didn't have. This forced them to reconsider their bootstrapping strategy and pursue funding, leading to a two-month San Francisco fundraising effort that ultimately didn't land the right investment.

episode_title: From blogger to billionaire, Canva's co-founder on what failures at Google Wave taught him
question: How many people are currently using Canva and what is Cameron Adams' vision for future growth?
transcript_excerpt: Canva currently has 250 million people using the product. Despite all the efforts over 14 years and 5,000 people joining the company, Cameron believes they have only scratched the surface of what Canva can do. He strongly believes that over a billion people should be using it all around the world, and that is what the company is building for.

episode_title: From blogger to billionaire, Canva's co-founder on what failures at Google Wave taught him
question: How has Canva integrated artificial intelligence into its product and what was the user response?
transcript_excerpt: Canva has integrated AI across all of its product as a way to enable creativity, help users get started quicker, and assist when they get stuck. The company has had over 30 billion uses of its AI features to date. When they rolled out a major second version of Canva AI earlier this year, it was so popular that they could barely keep up with the demand, forcing them to manage the rollout carefully.

episode_title: From blogger to billionaire, Canva's co-founder on what failures at Google Wave taught him
question: What is Canva's two-step plan and how does the company apply its moral thread beyond shareholder value?
transcript_excerpt: Canva's two-step plan is: step one is to make a valuable company, and step two is to do the most good the company can in the world. This means sending positive ripples all around the world through the product and through the Canva Foundation, which focuses on delivering basic needs and quality education to everyone. Cameron and his wife also joined the Giving Pledge in 2025, committing the majority of their wealth to protecting nature and conserving and regenerating biodiversity around the planet.
